name: Rum - Product Unspecified (EU category 1 bound)
abv_market: EU (legal minimum, not a product value)

sugar_bound.rule: EU 2019/787 Annex I cat. 1(f): <=20 g sweetening products/L as invert sugar

source.title: Regulation (EU) 2019/787 on spirit drinks, Annex I (Categories of spirit drinks)

quote: The minimum alcoholic strength by volume of rum shall be 37,5 %. ... Rum may be sweetened in order to round off the final taste. However, the final product may not contain more than 20 grams of sweetening products per litre, expressed as invert sugar.
notes: Regulatory upper bound only (0-20 g/L invert-sugar equivalent = 0-2.0 g/100 mL); actual sugar product-specific and often ~0. Binds only rum sold as 'rum' in the EU/UK; US-market rum is not bound by this rule. ABV product-specific (EU minimum 37.5%). Caramel allowed only for colour; rum shall not be flavoured, so spiced rum is outside this category.

name: Whisky/Whiskey - Product Unspecified (EU category 2)
abv_market: EU (legal minimum, not a product value)

sugar_bound.rule: EU 2019/787 Annex I cat. 2(d): shall not be sweetened; only plain caramel E150a

source.title: Regulation (EU) 2019/787 on spirit drinks, Annex I (Categories of spirit drinks)
source.locator: Annex I, category 2 (Whisky or whiskey), points (a), (b), (d)

quote: The final distillate, to which only water and plain caramel (for colouring) may be added ... The minimum alcoholic strength by volume of whisky or whiskey shall be 40 %. ... Whisky or whiskey shall not be sweetened, even for rounding off the taste, or flavoured, or contain any additives other than plain caramel (E 150a) used for adjusting the colour.
notes: No sweetening permitted: sugar bound 0 g/L (E150a caramel only, a colouring amount). Applies to Irish whiskey (EU GI in this category) and any whisky marketed in the EU. US bourbon/rye have their own profiles (ip_bourbon_generic etc.). ABV product-specific (min 40%).

notes: Only water and plain caramel may be added: sugar bound 0 g/L. ABV product-specific (legal minimum 40%).

name: Flavoured Vodka - Product Unspecified (EU category 31)

sugar_bound.rule: EU 2019/787 Annex I cat. 31(d): <100 g/L as invert sugar when sweetened

source.title: Regulation (EU) 2019/787 on spirit drinks, Annex I (Categories of spirit drinks)

quote: The minimum alcoholic strength by volume of flavoured vodka shall be 37,5 %. (c) Flavoured vodka may be sweetened, blended, flavoured, matured or coloured. (d) When flavoured vodka is sweetened, the final product shall contain less than 100 grams of sweetening products per litre, expressed as invert sugar.
notes: Wide bound: 0 to <10 g/100 mL. Real products range from unsweetened (e.g. Absolut Citron per OHLQ copy) to liqueur-adjacent; product must be named for a usable sugar value. House infusions (apricot-infused vodka) are not mapped here.

name: Old Tom Gin - Product Unspecified (sweetened gin, no legal cap)
abv_market: EU (legal minimum, not a product value)

source.title: Regulation (EU) 2019/787 on spirit drinks, Annex I (Categories of spirit drinks)

quote: The minimum alcoholic strength by volume of gin shall be 37,5 %. ... The term 'gin' may be supplemented by the term 'dry' if it does not contain added sweetening exceeding 0,1 grams of sweetening products per litre of the final product, expressed as invert sugar.
notes: WORKING MODEL. EU gin (cat. 20) sets no maximum sweetening for a gin not labelled 'dry'; the only limit is the 0.1 g/L threshold to use 'dry'. So Old Tom sugar is unbounded by law and UNRESOLVED until a product's sugar is published. sugar_bound left null deliberately. Brand example: ip_haymans_old_tom_gin_us (ABV only).

name: Cachaça - Product Unspecified (Brazil)
abv_market: Brazil (legal range 38-48% vol at 20 C, not a product value)

sugar_bound.rule: Decreto 6.871/2009 (cachaça definition): açúcares até 6 g/L; 6-30 g/L = 'cachaça adoçada'. Decree since revoked by Decreto 12.709/2025

source.title: Decreto nº 6.871, de 4 de junho de 2009
source.locator: cachaça definition and §1 (cachaça adoçada); page header 'Revogado pelo Decreto nº 12.709, de 2025'

quote: Cachaça é a denominação típica e exclusiva da aguardente de cana produzida no Brasil, com graduação alcoólica de trinta e oito a quarenta e oito por cento em volume, a vinte graus Celsius, obtida pela destilação do mosto fermentado do caldo de cana-de-açúcar com características sensoriais peculiares, podendo ser adicionada de açúcares até seis gramas por litro. § 1 o A cachaça que contiver açúcares em quantidade superior a seis gramas por litro e inferior a trinta gramas por litro será denominada de cachaça adoçada.
notes: Bound <=0.6 g/100 mL for unsweetened cachaça. CAVEAT: the planalto page marks Decreto 6.871 as revoked by Decreto 12.709/2025. The current decree (https://www.planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/_Ato2023-2026/2025/Decreto/D12709.htm, scraped) keeps the 38-48% vol definition ('Cachaça é a denominação típica e exclusiva da aguardente de cana produzida na República Federativa do Brasil, com graduação alcoólica de 38% (trinta e oito por cento) a 48% (quarenta e oito por cento) em volume, a 20 °C (vinte graus Celsius), com características sensoriais peculiares.') but the extracted text did not state the sugar limit; it may now sit in a MAPA ordinance. Treat 6 g/L as the historical/likely-current rule, not re-verified.
